tracks.title: Concerto No. 11 in D minor, RV 565
And the glory of the Lord
Thus saith the Lord of hosts
But who may abide the day of His coming
And he shall purify the sons of Levi
O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion
For behold, darkness shall cover the earth
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light
For unto us a child is born
There were shepherds abiding in the fields
And lo, the angel of the Lord
And the angel said unto them
And suddenly there was with the angel
Glory to God in the highest
Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion
Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened
He shall feed his flock like a shepherd
He was despised and rejected of men
Surely he hath borne our griefs and carried our sorrows
And with his stripes we are healed
All we like sheep have gone astray
All they that see him laugh to scorn
He trusted in God that he would deliver him
Thy rebuke hath broken his heart
Behold and see if there be any sorrow
But thou didst not leave his soul in hell
Lift up your heads, O ye gates
Let all the angels of God worship Him
Thou art gone up on high
Why do the nations so furiously rage together
Let us break their bonds asunder
Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron
I know that my Redeemer liveth
Behold, I tell you a mystery
Then shall be brought to pass
O death, where is thy sting
If God be for us, who can be against us

people.description: London chamber orchestra founded by Neville Marriner in 1958, named after the church of St Martin-in-the-Fields where it first played.
people.name: Academy of St Martin in the Fields

people.description: German countertenor, among the best known of his voice since the 1990s, in Bach, Handel and Vivaldi above all.
people.name: Andreas Scholl

people.description: Spanish-born American guitarist, the youngest son of Celedonio Romero, of the Romeros guitar quartet.
people.name: Angel Romero

people.description: Venetian composer, violinist and priest, nicknamed "the Red Priest" for his hair. He wrote hundreds of concertos, many for the girls of the Ospedale della Pietà orphanage where he taught, and his three-movement fast–slow–fast form shaped the Baroque concerto.
people.name: Antonio Vivaldi

people.description: Hungarian conductor who led the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra and the Berlin Philharmonic at the same time, from 1895 until his death. He was also a fine pianist, and in 1906 recorded piano rolls for the Welte-Mignon reproducing piano.
people.name: Arthur Nikisch

people.description: Italian pianist and harpsichordist, a chamber partner of Salvatore Accardo and many others.
people.name: Bruno Canino

people.description: Chamber orchestra led by the violinist Adolf Busch, which recorded Bach's Brandenburg Concertos in the 1930s.
people.name: Busch Chamber Players

people.description: Swiss Baroque violinist, who founded and led Ensemble 415.
people.name: Chiara Banchini

people.description: French composer whose harmony and tone colour — whole-tone scales, unresolved chords, music built from sound and atmosphere — opened the way to twentieth-century music. He disliked the label "Impressionist" it earned him.
people.name: Claude Debussy

people.description: American organist, born in Minneapolis, who settled in Germany in the 1960s and made a series of Bach and Handel organ recordings for Philips.
people.name: Daniel Chorzempa

people.description: Period-instrument ensemble founded in Geneva by Chiara Banchini, named after the pitch it plays at, A = 415 Hz.
people.name: Ensemble 415

people.description: Swiss choir founded by Michel Corboz in 1961.
people.name: Ensemble vocal de Lausanne

people.description: The Catalonia College of Music, a conservatory in Barcelona founded in 2001 and housed in L'Auditori, whose students and teachers perform as its ensembles.
people.name: Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya

people.description: Italian violinist and teacher, who often played with Salvatore Accardo.
people.name: Franco Gulli

people.description: Viennese composer who wrote over six hundred songs as well as symphonies, chamber music and piano works, nearly all of it before his death at thirty-one.
people.name: Franz Schubert

people.description: Polish composer and pianist who settled in Paris in 1831. Almost everything he wrote is for solo piano — ballades, nocturnes, études, mazurkas and polonaises — and it changed what the instrument could sing.
people.name: Frédéric Chopin

people.description: German composer, among the most prolific in history, who worked in Leipzig and Frankfurt and from 1721 in Hamburg as music director of its five principal churches. Better known in his lifetime than Bach, he was a friend of his and godfather to Carl Philipp Emanuel.
people.name: Georg Philipp Telemann

people.description: German-born composer who made his career in London, writing Italian operas for the stage and then English oratorios such as Messiah. He became a British subject in 1727 and is buried in Westminster Abbey.
people.name: George Frideric Handel

people.description: German conductor and champion of new music, who gave the premiere of Berg's Violin Concerto in 1936 and in the 1950s recorded much of the Baroque and Classical repertoire.
people.name: Hermann Scherchen

people.description: French-born violinist who led orchestras in North America, for many years as concertmaster of the Toronto Symphony Orchestra.
people.name: Jacques Israelievitch

people.description: German composer and organist who spent most of his career in Weimar, Köthen and, from 1723, Leipzig, as cantor of St Thomas. His keyboard, organ, choral and orchestral music sums up the Baroque, and his counterpoint has been studied by every generation since.
people.name: Johann Sebastian Bach

people.description: German composer and pianist who worked mostly in Vienna. He wrote four symphonies, concertos, chamber music, songs and A German Requiem, holding to Classical forms through the Romantic era.
people.name: Johannes Brahms

people.description: American composer whose library of royalty-free music at incompetech.com, under Creative Commons licences, is heard in thousands of films, videos and games.
people.name: Kevin MacLeod

people.description: German-Japanese pianist. Her Open Goldberg Variations and Open Well-Tempered Clavier were crowdfunded and released into the public domain, recordings and scores alike.
people.name: Kimiko Ishizaka

people.description: English Baroque flautist, who played with The English Concert through the 1980s.
people.name: Lisa Beznosiuk

people.description: London orchestra founded in 1904 as a self-governing company of its players, resident at the Barbican Centre since 1982.
people.name: London Symphony Orchestra

people.description: Composer and pianist born in Bonn who settled in Vienna. His nine symphonies, 32 piano sonatas and string quartets bridge the Classical and Romantic eras, and he kept composing after he had lost his hearing.
people.name: Ludwig van Beethoven

people.description: Dutch countertenor, who founded PRJCT Amsterdam and directs it.
people.name: Maarten Engeltjes

people.description: English Baroque violinist, of The English Concert and other period orchestras.
people.name: Micaela Comberti

people.description: Swiss choral conductor who founded the Ensemble vocal de Lausanne in 1961 and recorded much of the Baroque sacred repertoire with it for Erato.
people.name: Michel Corboz

people.description: Swiss chamber orchestra founded in Lausanne in 1942 by Victor Desarzens.
people.name: Orchestre de chambre de Lausanne

people.description: Period-instrument orchestra and choir founded in Amsterdam by the countertenor Maarten Engeltjes.
people.name: PRJCT Amsterdam

people.description: Cellist born in Sheffield to a Sri Lankan family, for many years in the Arditti Quartet.
people.name: Rohan de Saram

people.description: Italian violinist, who won the Paganini Competition in 1958, known for Paganini and the Italian Baroque.
people.name: Salvatore Accardo

people.description: English Baroque violinist, leader of The English Concert from its early years.
people.name: Simon Standage

people.description: London period-instrument orchestra founded by Trevor Pinnock in 1972, whose Vivaldi, Bach and Handel recordings for Archiv helped make Baroque music on old instruments ordinary.
people.name: The English Concert

people.description: English harpsichordist and conductor, who founded The English Concert in 1972 and directed it from the keyboard until 2003.
people.name: Trevor Pinnock

people.description: "The President's Own", founded by Act of Congress in 1798: the oldest professional musical organisation in the United States, whose mission is to play for the President.
people.name: United States Marine Band

works.description: A companion to the Sinfonia al Santo Sepolcro: a short sonata in the style of a church sonata, slow and grave.
works.title: Sonata al Santo Sepolcro in E-Flat Major

works.description: A brief, sombre sinfonia "at the Holy Sepulchre", meant for Holy Week, built on slow chromatic lines.
works.title: Sinfonia al Santo Sepolcro in B Minor

works.description: Spring, the first of the four violin concertos Vivaldi published in 1725 as part of Il cimento dell'armonia e dell'inventione, each set to a sonnet: birdsong, a murmuring brook, a sleeping goatherd and his barking dog.
works.title: The Four Seasons, Concerto No. 1 "Spring"

works.description: Autumn, the third of The Four Seasons: peasants celebrating the harvest with wine and dancing, a drowsy slow movement, and a dawn hunt.
works.title: The Four Seasons, Concerto No. 3 "Autumn"

works.description: Winter, the last of The Four Seasons: shivering in icy wind and chattering teeth, rain heard from beside the fire, and walking carefully over the ice.
works.title: The Four Seasons, Concerto No. 4 "Winter"

works.description: Summer, the second of The Four Seasons: heat-weary stillness, the cuckoo and turtledove, swarming flies, and a hailstorm that flattens the crops.
works.title: The Four Seasons, Concerto No. 2 "Summer"

works.description: From L'estro armonico, Op. 3: the only concerto in the set for one solo violin, short and direct, and the one nearly every young violinist learns.
works.title: L'estro armonico, Concerto No. 6 in A Minor

works.description: One of Vivaldi's cello concertos, written when the cello was only beginning to be heard as a solo instrument.
works.title: Cello Concerto in G Major

works.description: A short, bright concerto for mandolin and strings, among the best known of the few Vivaldi wrote for the instrument.
works.title: Mandolin Concerto in C Major

works.description: From Op. 10: the goldfinch, whose song the flute imitates in trills and flourishes.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 3 in D Major "Il gardellino"

works.description: The first of the six flute concertos of Vivaldi's Op. 10, published in 1728, the first set of concertos ever printed for the transverse flute: a storm at sea.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 1 in F Major "La tempesta di mare"

works.description: The fifth of the six flute concertos of Vivaldi's Op. 10.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 5 in F Major

works.description: The fourth of the six flute concertos of Vivaldi's Op. 10.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 4 in G Major

works.description: The last of the six flute concertos of Vivaldi's Op. 10.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 6 in G Major

works.description: From Op. 10: a night of ghosts and sleep, in movements titled "Fantasmi" and "Il sonno", the sleep one hushed over muted strings.
works.title: Flute Concerto No. 2 in G Minor "La notte"

works.description: One of the many concertos Vivaldi wrote for bassoon — more than three dozen — giving the instrument agile solo writing rare for its time.
works.title: Bassoon Concerto in A Minor

works.description: From L'estro armonico, Op. 3: a concerto for two violins that Bach arranged for organ as BWV 593.
works.title: L'estro armonico, Concerto No. 8 in A Minor

works.description: Vivaldi's concerto for two mandolins, the soloists answering each other over strings, with a gentle, plucked slow movement.
works.title: Concerto for Two Mandolins in G Major

works.description: A concerto pairing two oboes as soloists, in Vivaldi's usual fast–slow–fast design.
works.title: Concerto for Two Oboes in A Minor

works.description: A concerto for an unusually large group of soloists — recorders, mandolins, theorbos, violins in tromba marina, cello — written for a state visit to the Ospedale della Pietà in 1740.
works.title: Concerto in C Major for Many Instruments

works.description: From L'estro armonico, Op. 3: a concerto for two violins and cello whose first movement leads, after a short Adagio, into a fugue — one of the pieces Bach arranged for organ (BWV 596).
works.title: L'estro armonico, Concerto No. 11 in D Minor

works.description: From L'estro armonico, Op. 3 (1711), the set that made Vivaldi famous across Europe: a concerto for four violins that Bach later arranged for four harpsichords.
works.title: L'estro armonico, Concerto No. 10 in B Minor

works.description: The best known of Vivaldi's sacred works: a setting of the Gloria in twelve short movements for soloists, choir and orchestra, probably written for the girls of the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice. It was rediscovered in the 1920s and first performed again in 1939.
works.title: Gloria in D Major

works.description: A setting of Psalm 127 for alto and strings, in nine movements: the fourth, "Cum dederit", a long, hushed lullaby over muted strings, is among the most famous things Vivaldi wrote.
works.title: Nisi Dominus in G Minor

works.description: Vivaldi's setting of the Magnificat, the Song of Mary, for choir, soloists and strings, in short contrasting sections.
works.title: Magnificat in G Minor

works.description: A setting of the first ten verses of the Stabat Mater for alto and strings, written for a church in Brescia in 1712: one of Vivaldi's earliest surviving sacred works, slow and grave throughout.
works.title: Stabat Mater in F Minor

works.description: The last of the twelve trio sonatas of Vivaldi's Op. 1, published in 1705: twenty variations for two violins and continuo on La Follia, the dance tune Corelli had set a few years before.
works.title: Trio Sonata in D Minor "La Follia"
Sonata in F major, RV 68
Sonata in F major, RV 70
Sonata in G major, RV 71
Sonata in B flat major, RV 77

works.description: A setting of Psalm 110 for soloists, double choir and orchestra, identified as Vivaldi's only in 2005, after it had long been attributed to Baldassare Galuppi.
works.title: Dixit Dominus in D Major

works.description: A sonata for violin, cello and continuo, the two string parts in conversation over the bass.
works.title: Sonata in C minor, RV 83

works.description: A sonata for recorder, bassoon and continuo, the bassoon a partner to the recorder rather than only its bass.
works.title: Sonata in A minor, RV 86

works.description: A chamber concerto for lute, two violins and continuo, written in the 1730s for the Bohemian count Johann Joseph von Wrtby. Its Largo has made it a favourite of guitarists, who play it more often than lutenists do.
works.title: Lute Concerto in D Major

works.description: A piano suite in four movements — Prélude, Menuet, Clair de lune and Passepied — begun around 1890 and published in 1905. Clair de lune takes its name from a Verlaine poem.
works.title: Suite bergamasque

works.description: Four impromptus for piano, written in 1827, the year before Schubert died; the third, in G-flat major, is a long, singing melody over rippling accompaniment.
works.title: Four Impromptus

works.description: The first of Chopin's four ballades, completed in about 1835: a single-movement piano narrative that grows from a hesitant opening to a stormy coda.
works.title: Ballade No. 1 in G Minor

works.description: Chopin's second ballade, dedicated to Robert Schumann, which sets a gentle, rocking theme against sudden furious outbursts.
works.title: Ballade No. 2 in F Major

works.description: The quartet of the first Production of the Musique de table (1733), for flute, oboe, violin and continuo.
works.title: Tafelmusik I: Quartet in G major

works.description: The concerto of the first Production of the Musique de table (1733), with flute, violin and cello as soloists before strings and continuo.
works.title: Tafelmusik I: Concerto in A major

works.description: The suite that opens the first of the three Productions of Telemann's Musique de table, published by subscription in Hamburg in 1733: a French overture and a run of dances, for two flutes, strings and continuo.
works.title: Tafelmusik I: Ouverture-Suite in E minor

works.description: The first of the three suites of Water Music, written for George I's barge trip on the Thames in July 1717, played by musicians on a boat alongside.
works.title: Water Music Suite No. 1 in F Major

works.description: The second Water Music suite, with trumpets and horns — music to carry outdoors over the water — including the famous Alla Hornpipe.
works.title: Water Music Suite No. 2 in D Major

works.description: The third Water Music suite, quieter and more intimate, with flute and recorder.
works.title: Water Music Suite No. 3 in G Major

works.description: Written for George II's celebration of the Peace of Aix-la-Chapelle in London's Green Park in 1749, for a large wind band. Twelve thousand people came to its public rehearsal.
works.title: Music for the Royal Fireworks

works.description: Handel's English oratorio on the life of Christ, to a libretto by Charles Jennens, composed in about three weeks in 1741 and first performed in Dublin in 1742. Its Hallelujah chorus closes Part II.
works.title: Messiah

works.description: The first of the six Brandenburg Concertos, which Bach sent to the Margrave of Brandenburg in 1721, each for a different group of instruments. This one has hunting horns, oboes and a violino piccolo.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 1 in F Major

works.description: The second Brandenburg Concerto, with a solo group of trumpet, recorder, oboe and violin; its high trumpet part is one of the hardest in the Baroque repertoire.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 2 in F Major

works.description: The third Brandenburg Concerto, for three groups of three strings — violins, violas and cellos — with only two chords standing in for a slow movement.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 in G Major

works.description: The fourth Brandenburg Concerto, for violin and two recorders ("echo flutes") with strings, the violin given dazzling solo passages.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G Major

works.description: The fifth Brandenburg Concerto, for flute, violin and harpsichord; its long harpsichord solo in the first movement is often called the first keyboard concerto.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 5 in D Major

works.description: The sixth Brandenburg Concerto, for low strings alone — two violas, two violas da gamba, cello and continuo — with no violins at all.
works.title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 6 in B-Flat Major

works.description: Probably the most famous organ piece ever written: a dramatic toccata around a fugue. Its date — and whether it is Bach's at all — has been debated by scholars.
works.title: Toccata and Fugue in D Minor

works.description: An organ fugue on two subjects from the second movement of Corelli's Trio Sonata Op. 3 No. 4, worked out at far greater length than Corelli's own.
works.title: Fugue in B Minor on a Theme by Corelli

works.description: Bach's arrangement for organ of Vivaldi's Concerto No. 8 from L'estro armonico (RV 522), made at Weimar: the two solo violins answer each other between two manuals, over the pedals.
works.title: Organ Concerto in A Minor (after Vivaldi)

works.description: The longest of Bach's Weimar concerto arrangements for organ, after Vivaldi's violin concerto "Il Grosso Mogul" (RV 208), the virtuoso violin cadenzas turned into passages for the organ, recitative included.
works.title: Organ Concerto in C Major (after Vivaldi)

works.description: Bach's arrangement for organ of Vivaldi's Concerto No. 11 from L'estro armonico (RV 565), made at Weimar around 1714–17 while he studied the Italian concerto. The two violins and cello are shared out between the hands and pedals; the fugue after the opening Adagio becomes a full organ fugue. The manuscript is in Bach's hand, but a note by his son Wilhelm Friedemann on it had the piece taken for the son's own until the twentieth century.
works.title: Organ Concerto in D Minor (after Vivaldi)

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key. This first prelude, all broken chords, is one of the best-known pieces in the keyboard repertoire.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 1 in C Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 2 in C Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 3 in C-Sharp Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key. Its fugue has five voices.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 4 in C-Sharp Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 5 in D Major

works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 6 in D Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 7 in E-Flat Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 8 in E-Flat Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 9 in E Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key. Its fugue is the only one in two voices.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 10 in E Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 11 in F Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 12 in F Minor

works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 13 in F-Sharp Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 14 in F-Sharp Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 15 in G Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 16 in G Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 17 in A-Flat Major

works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 19 in A Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 20 in A Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 21 in B-Flat Major

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key. Its fugue has five voices.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 22 in B-Flat Minor

works.description: From Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722), Bach's cycle of a prelude and fugue in every major and minor key.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 23 in B Major

works.description: The last prelude and fugue of Book I of The Well-Tempered Clavier (1722). Its fugue subject uses all twelve notes of the chromatic scale.
works.title: Prelude and Fugue No. 24 in B Minor

works.description: An aria followed by thirty variations on its bass line, published in 1741. Every third variation is a canon, at intervals growing from the unison to the ninth, and the aria returns at the end.
works.title: Goldberg Variations

works.description: Twenty-one lively dances based on Hungarian themes, first for piano four hands, which became some of Brahms's most popular music; No. 5 is the best known.
works.title: Hungarian Dances

works.description: A short piano bagatelle that was not published until 1867, forty years after Beethoven's death. Who "Elise" was is still unknown.
works.title: Für Elise
